fills.researcher_notes: Brief confirms the wiki's '30/36 inches' string flagged as 'Capacity' is a misparsed diameter, not a capacity value, so nothing is staged from it. Searched offshore-technology.com and nsenergybusiness.com (both have a dedicated market-data profile for the Wafa-Mellitah line but none for Defa-Brega), the 2024 OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin (downloaded and pdftotext'd asb-2024.pdf directly from opec.org, which resolved fine this session -- no Table 4.10-style gas-pipeline listing exists in this edition at all, and neither 'Defa' nor 'Brega' appear near any pipeline table), and Wikipedia (Raguba field, Zelten oil field -- both only describe a Zelten/Raguba-Brega OIL pipeline via Nasser field, not this gas line, and cite no operational specs). Gem.wiki's own single citation for this page is 'World Energy Atlas, Petroleum Economist, 2001' -- a print atlas, not a fetchable/verifiable URL, and not usable as a ref per protocol anyway. No independent diameter or capacity figure for the actual Defa-Brega Gas Pipeline was found. UNRESOLVED.

No commissioning-year source found for this specific pipeline. Defa oil/gas field was discovered by 1962 and is a long-producing Sirte Basin field, so the gas line is plausibly a 1970s-80s vintage gathering/trunk line, but I found no source that dates the pipeline itself (as opposed to the field). Did not find any Defa-Brega-specific coverage in Libya Herald/Libya Observer/Zawya archives (those cover the newer 2026 Farigh-Brega line, a different, later pipeline that ties into the same 42-inch Sirte Oil Company trunk network at Brega). UNRESOLVED.

validity.recommendation: Do NOT stage 'Mellitah Oil & Gas' as Operator for P0482, despite the brief's cluster-wide framing that Mellitah operates all six rows. Have a human weigh Waha Oil Company (upstream, produces at Defa field) vs Sirte Oil Company (midstream, operates the Brega hub and its gas trunk network) as the likelier Operator candidate -- I could not find a source naming an operator for this specific pipeline, so I'm not staging either without one.
validity.researcher_notes: Defa gas field is a Waha Oil Company asset (NOC 59.2% / Marathon 16.33% / ConocoPhillips 16.33% / Hess 8.2% JV) in the Sirte Basin -- confirmed via Wood Mackenzie 'Waha Operated Fields' listing and industryabout.com's Defa Oil Field profile. Brega is Sirte Oil Company's home base (SOC founded 1981 as the NOC subsidiary running the Brega petrochemical/gas hub) -- consistent with this row's sheet Owner already reading 'Libyan National Oil Corp [100.%]' (SOC is 100% NOC-owned, unlike the Waha JV or the Eni-NOC Mellitah JV). Both Waha and SOC are organizationally distinct from Mellitah Oil & Gas, the Eni-NOC 50:50 JV that runs the Western Libya Gas Project / Mellitah Complex covered by the other five rows in this cluster (Wafa, Bahr Assalam, E Structure, DP3-DP4-Sabratha) -- Mellitah's own site (mellitahog.ly) lists its operated fields as Wafa, Bahr Essalam, Bouri, Abu Attifel and El Feel; Defa/Brega is not among them. Separately, I found (via Ecofin Agency / Pipeline Technology Journal / Libya Observer coverage of the unrelated, newer 2026 Farigh-Brega Gas Pipeline) that gas from the Sirte Basin's Zueitina axis is injected into 'an existing 42-inch pipeline operated by the Sirte Oil and Gas Production and Manufacturing Company' feeding Brega -- i.e. SOC does operate at least one Sirte-Basin-to-Brega gas trunk, though I could not confirm this is the same 299 km line as GEM's 'Defa-Brega Gas Pipeline' specifically. Not staged as a fill because no source names an operator for the Defa-Brega line by name.
